newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Forrestania says more nickel at Emily.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Forrestania says more nickel at Emily.

text.p: Forrestania Gold NL said on Tuesday it had recorded further high-grade nickel intersections from drilling at its Emily Ann prospect in Western Australia.
The results firmly establish continuity of the ore horizon both along the strike and down dip zone of the test site, the company said in a report to the Australian Stock Exchange.

There were indications that there was at least an additional 100 metres of potential mineralisation beneath the test level, Forrestania said. One of the drill holes, RTD 27, intersected two zones of mineralisation in the most recent round of tests.
The upper zone returned results of 4.2 metres grading 5.0 percent nickel from 185.4 metres and the second zone returned 5.9 metres at 6.9 percent nickel from 211.4 metres, Forrestania said.
Another hole RTD 28, returned 11.0 metres grading 2.3 percent nickel from 212.96 metres, including 8.0 metres at 2.9 percent nickel from 212.96 metres.
The Emily Ann prospect is within the Roundtop project, a joint venture between the Lake Johnston Joint Venture Partners, with 75 percent, and Capricorn Resources Australia NL which has 25 percent.
Forrestania and South Africa's Gencor Ltd are 50-50 partners in the Lake Johnston Joint Venture.
The Emily Ann prospect is located about three km north of the Maggie hays nickel deposit, where Forrestania and Gencor are spending A$10.6 million on exploration work.
